answer: Physical Presence Pulse Registry: each agent must return a hardware-timed pulse challenge from a tamper-resistant radio beacon bound to one fixed location, and the registry accepts a new identity only after that beacon’s unique clock drift is observed across a randomized spiral of three sampling windows. Because one operator cannot occupy many physically distinct beacon sites, each extra identity forces a separate site, device, and maintenance visit; a Sybil batch of n identities pays n site leases plus n installation trips, and any beacon can harbor only one live registration at a time.
